fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 has an exact degree blind spot: a parity perturbation on k+1 variables has zero mass and zero marginals on every subset of size at most k, while a k-perfect family guarantees injectivity only through k variables. Its four-variable k=4 test avoids this asymptotic obstruction and therefore cannot discriminate the claimed log-width mechanism; no theorem converts anchor excess into support on at most k variables.

Proposal 2 does not escape affine linearity under unrestricted selectors: precomputed nonlinear phase labels become a fixed linear column map, so G13 coefficient-sum-one affine combinations remain affine combinations after lifting. The Construction-A4 basis, carries, target, weights, control, and unrestricted CVP objective are unfrozen, and merely scoring G7/G11/G12/G13 is not a G6-compliant experiment.

Proposal 3 confuses high girth with signed-flow soundness: high girth excludes short word collisions but not integer combinations of many endpoint tags or splices having the same tag totals. Variable endpoint unit vectors also create the G12 dilemma—zero-centered equal norms make drops cheaper—while no explicit group, transition-word map, target, normalization, control, or complete unrestricted fiber is specified.

Proposal 4 is algebraically blocked by Lawrence lifting itself. In the standard higher Lawrence kernel, every z in ker(A) yields the bounded-type move (z,-z,0,...), so shared-sum rows preserve type-two circuits rather than forcing type to grow; G7, G13, and G19 lifts therefore remain live, and baseline replication supplies no relative-gap law.

Proposal 5 supplies no polynomial-size useful-degree bound: full squarefree degree on three variables is a constant exhaustive encoding, whereas degree growing with n gives n^Omega(d) Macaulay dimension absent a proved ABP compression valid for unrestricted integral functionals. The degree weights, target, control, and exact CVP shell are also unspecified, so the proposed test cannot distinguish G20/G21 scaling.

Proposal 6 tests only coefficients in [-2,2], contrary to unrestricted CVP; with a variable Gram matrix and no normalized eigenvalue bound, competitors outside that box cannot be excluded. One- and two-clause Delaunay feasibility would not establish overlap preservation, defeat G13/G19 globally, or produce a growing shell ratio.

Proposal 7 cannot emit Plucker minors of an unknown lattice combination as linear CVP coordinates. Precomputed column wedges only give a linear sum of individual tags, not the wedge or minors of the combined port state, so unrestricted signed coefficients retain G13/G19 cancellations and G22 entangled vectors.
